answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every identity must earn trust through a chain of small verified jobs, each receipt hash-linked to the last, so a newcomer starts as an isolated island with no credit and cannot buy reputation. New accounts must also lock a refundable deposit before transacting, and one forged receipt slashes it, leaving only an umber trace of the stake. Reputation then grows at a glacier's pace — slow, verifiable, and impossible to fake in bulk — so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand deposits and a thousand jobs, and forgery pays less than honest work.
